title: Monet, with added lasers
summary_es: Un crítico de radio reseña con mucha ironía una exposición «inmersiva» sobre Monet y la compara con un cuadro de verdad.
prediction_prompt: Have you ever been to an "immersive" exhibition? What might a traditional art critic say about one?

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: I have just spent forty minutes standing inside a painting, and I am not sure I shall ever recover.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: "Monet: The Immersion" has arrived in a former warehouse by the river.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Tickets cost thirty-two pounds, which, I was assured, includes the lasers.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: You enter through a corridor of artificial mist, presumably so that you cannot see what you have paid for.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Then the main hall opens up, and I will admit, grudgingly, that the first thirty seconds are impressive.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Water lilies the size of buses drift across the walls, the floor and, inevitably, the visitors.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: A small child next to me tried to pick one up. I envied her optimism.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: After that, the problems begin, and they do not stop.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: The paintings have been animated. Clouds move. Bridges wobble. A haystack, for reasons unknown, catches fire.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: All this is accompanied by music that sounds like a piano falling slowly down a staircase.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: At one point a voice announces, in a reverent whisper, that Monet "painted with light".

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: He painted with paint. It is one of the few things about him we know for certain.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Now, I have no objection to technology in a gallery.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: What I object to is the assumption that a masterpiece needs improving.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Monet spent thirty years looking at the same pond precisely because it did not move.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Or rather, because it moved so subtly that only a lifetime of attention could catch it.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: To make his water ripple for us is to do our looking for us, and to do it badly.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: The organisers say the show "brings art to people who find museums intimidating".

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: It is a generous aim, and I do not wish to mock it.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: But I counted eleven people filming the walls and none simply watching them.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: If museums are intimidating, a dark room full of telephones is hardly the cure.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: There is, to be fair, one genuinely good idea.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Near the exit, a small side room shows a single real canvas, borrowed for the season.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: It is a modest painting of poplars, about the size of a kitchen window. It does not move at all.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: I stood in front of it for ten minutes. For most of that time, I was alone.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: Everything the main hall had shouted, this little picture said quietly, and said better.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: A woman came in, glanced at it, and asked the attendant where the gift shop was.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: The gift shop, I can report, is magnificent. It may well be the true heart of the enterprise.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: You can buy a water-lily umbrella, a water-lily phone case and, less explicably, water-lily socks.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: I bought the socks. I am not proud of it, but they are extremely comfortable.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: So, should you go? If you have children under ten, possibly. They will run about and be happy.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: If you love Monet, I would gently suggest the train to an actual museum.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: It costs less, the paintings stay still, and nobody will set fire to a haystack.

segments.speaker: julian
segments.text: "Monet: The Immersion" runs until the end of August. The poplars, I suspect, will outlast it.
